clue.text: Source established beyond doubt by an English church

parts.note: something established beyond doubt has been proven
taken as written
CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A claim about origins is said to be confirmed by an English church.
explanation.definitionFit: Provenance is the place of origin or record of where something came from, its source.

clue.text: Leave theatrical role

definitions.meaning: an actor's role in a play

explanation.surface: Abandon a stage part.
explanation.definitionFit: To part is to go away from someone; a part is also an actor's role.

clue.text: Element of initiation ceremony in days gone by

indicators.note: Element of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of an initiation rite from long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, at some time in the past.

clue.text: Property in car

definitions.meaning: a car with a long body and rear door for loads

explanation.surface: Assets held in an automobile.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a landed property; an estate car is a roomy family vehicle.

clue.text: Star involved with the official dogmatic statements

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters are tangled together into a new order

explanation.surface: A celebrity mixes with an official to issue rigid pronouncements.
explanation.definitionFit: Articles of faith are fixed tenets of belief, statements of doctrine held without question.

clue.text: Revolutionary's engaging soldiers for tedious tasks

indicators.note: engaging means taking in, so the soldiers go inside

parts.note: Che Guevara is the crossword's usual revolutionary, here with possessive s
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A rebel hires troops to do the dull jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: The revolutionary is Che Guevara; 'engaging' reads as charming but here means taking in.
explanation.definitionFit: Chores are routine household jobs, typically dull duties.

clue.text: Keen Conservative coming in to help

indicators.note: the Conservative abbreviation enters the word for help, sitting within it

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: An eager Tory arrives to lend a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen and acid both describe something sharp or cutting, as in a keen or acid wit.

clue.text: Confinement of prisoners with exercise given minimal time

parts.note: cons are convicts
to train is to exercise

indicators.note: minimal says take only the smallest part, the first letter of time

explanation.surface: Inmates confined and allowed little time for exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Constraint is restriction or limitation, the state of being held in check.

clue.text: Dry red soil scattered all over the place

indicators.note: scattered tells us the letters of dry red soil are strewn about

explanation.surface: Parched earth is strewn everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Disorderly means untidy and chaotic, the idiom all over the place.

clue.text: Soldiers given official recognition — something read out

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a common crossword abbreviation for soldiers
a citation is an official mention of bravery in dispatches

explanation.surface: Troops receive a formal commendation, which is read aloud to them.
explanation.definitionFit: A recitation is a piece spoken aloud from memory or from a text, something read out.

clue.text: Animals celebrated, rolling over

indicators.note: rolling over turns the word for celebrated back to front

parts.note: celebrated in song means sung

explanation.surface: Creatures that were fêted are tumbling about.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnus, or wildebeest, are African antelopes, an example of animals.

clue.text: Quiet little man will accept order, I forecast

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: the short name takes the order and I inside itself

parts.note: Ron is a short form of the man's name Ronald
an edict is an official order

explanation.surface: A shy small fellow agrees to an instruction, I predict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is not part of the definition; it goes in with the order, leaving 'forecast' as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A prediction is a statement of what will happen, a forecast.

clue.text: Hazel has such a small bit in play, speaking only at the start

indicators.note: in play means the letters are moving freely and can be rearranged
only the opening letter of speaking is used

explanation.surface: An actress named Hazel has a tiny part with lines only at the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in play' rearranges A SMALL BIT; 'only at the start' takes S from speaking. Hazel is the tree, not an actress.
explanation.definitionFit: The dangling catkins of the hazel tree are popularly called lambs' tails.

clue.text: Label for killer of pigs?

definitions.meaning: one who sticks pigs, i.e. slaughters them with a knife

explanation.surface: A tag for a butcher's man.
explanation.definitionFit: A gummed label is a sticker; someone who sticks pigs is, whimsically, a sticker too.

clue.text: Weapon made sir nasty

indicators.note: nasty suggests the letters of made sir are turned ugly and rearranged

explanation.surface: A firearm has turned a knight vicious.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidearm is a pistol or sword carried at the side, a personal weapon.

clue.text: Bill may get such an acknowledgement

definitions.text: Bill may get such an acknowledgement

parts.words: Bill may get such an acknowledgement
parts.note: a paid invoice is stamped to acknowledge that payment was received; Bill looks like a man's name

explanation.surface: A man called Bill might be thanked like this.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill is the invoice, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A written note confirming that money or goods have been received is given when a bill is paid.

clue.text: I dare somehow to conceal love as travelling supporter

indicators.note: the jumbled letters hide the love symbol inside them
somehow says the letters of I dare are reworked in some way

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A dare to keep an affair secret, posed to a supporter on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges I DARE to RADIE, and 'to conceal' puts O inside it after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadie travels with a touring band, setting up and supporting their equipment.

clue.text: Dog — one posing a problem?

definitions.meaning: a breed of gundog, such as the Irish red
the compiler of a crossword sets the puzzle for solvers

explanation.surface: A dog is the source of some difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter is both a gundog breed and the person who sets a puzzle.

clue.text: Book with more than one title

definitions.text: Book with more than one title

parts.words: Book with more than one title
parts.note: not a book with alternative names but a reference work listing many titled nobles

explanation.surface: A book published under several names.
explanation.walkthrough: The title here is a rank of nobility, not a book's name.
explanation.definitionFit: This reference guide lists the British aristocracy and their many hereditary titles.

clue.text: Provides refreshment in a variety of crates

indicators.note: a variety means a different arrangement of the letters of crates

explanation.surface: Drinks are supplied in several kinds of box.
explanation.definitionFit: To cater is to supply food and drink, so a host who caters provides refreshment.

clue.text: Bribe offered by cheat upsettingly exposed in tabloid

indicators.note: exposed in the paper means appearing inside the tabloid's name

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

indicators.note: upsettingly turns the word for cheat upside down, which in a down clue reads it backwards

parts.note: to rob is to cheat someone of something

explanation.surface: A bribe from a swindler, revealed to his dismay in a red-top newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsettingly' turns the cheat upside down, which in a down clue means read backwards; The Sun is a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: To suborn is to induce someone, by bribery, to commit perjury or another wrong.

clue.text: Lapsing somehow not good — backbone's needed

indicators.note: somehow says the remaining letters are rearranged
not tells us to leave out the letter for good

explanation.surface: Falling short morally, a person needs some backbone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not good' drops G from LAPSING, leaving LAPSIN, which 'somehow' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinal is the adjective for the spine, so it means of the backbone.

clue.text: Old city disciple embraces a US soldier turning up

indicators.note: embraces means holds within, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: a son can mean a follower or disciple, as in a son of the church

indicators.note: turning up reads the soldier upwards, backwards in a down clue

parts.note: GI is an American enlisted soldier

explanation.surface: A follower hugs an American serviceman who arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' in a down clue reads the soldier from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Saigon was the former name of Ho Chi Minh City in Vietnam, so an old city name.

clue.text: Water often flows over this to submerge floor covering for Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two pieces exchange their starts

parts.note: to flood is to submerge
a mat covers part of a floor

explanation.surface: Something tides wash over, said to drown a rug.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of FLOOD and MAT gives the sounds of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of muddy coast is covered by the tide at high water and exposed at low.

clue.text: One little girl, the flower of Oxford

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
sis is short for sister, a little girl in the family

explanation.surface: A single small girl is the pride of Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: A flower is something that flows, a river: the Thames is called this name where it runs through Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: The stretch of the Thames at Oxford is known by this name, so it is the river of that city.

clue.text: Native American dance on island

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: An indigenous dance performed on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hopi are a Native American people of north-eastern Arizona.

clue.text: Composer making request, right to interrupt

indicators.note: the right abbreviation breaks into the word for request

parts.note: to beg is to request

explanation.surface: A musician makes a plea, and someone correct cuts in.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer of the Second Viennese School.

clue.text: Action of one returning after journey is becoming very clear

definitions.text: Action of one returning after journey
definitions.meaning: arriving back at one's house after travelling
the idiom for a truth that finally strikes someone

explanation.surface: Returning from a trip makes things plain.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a return to one's house; idiomatically, a fact hitting home as it becomes clear.

clue.text: Piano seems to drown this organ

indicators.note: the words piano seems submerge the answer within them, so it runs hidden across them

explanation.surface: A piano is loud enough to overwhelm this instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' reads as the musical instrument; it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The nose is a bodily organ, the one used for smelling.

clue.text: Delightful singing by chaps heading off

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of the word for chaps is removed

parts.note: chaps are men
chanting is a kind of singing

explanation.surface: Men's singing is charming as they head off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes M from MEN, leaving EN; 'by' places it beside the singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enchanting charms and delights, as if casting a spell.
